name: Ezekiel

facts.author: Ezekiel the priest, the son of Buzi, who was taken to Babylon with King Jehoiachin and wrote down what God showed him (1:1-3).

about: Ezekiel was a priest who lived among the Jewish exiles by the river Chebar in Babylon. In the fifth year of King Jehoiachin's captivity he saw a great vision of the glory of God, with living creatures, wheels full of eyes and a throne like sapphire (1:26-28). God sent him to a rebellious people and made him a watchman for Israel (3:17).

Before Jerusalem fell, Ezekiel warned that the city would be destroyed, often acting out his messages with signs. In a vision he saw idols worshipped in the temple and the glory of the LORD leaving it (10:18). When his wife died, he was told not to mourn, as a sign to the people (24:15-18). Then news came that the city had fallen (33:21).

After that his message turned to hope. God Himself would shepherd His people, give them a new heart and a new spirit (36:26), and bring them back to life like the dry bones that rose up as a great army (37:10). The book ends with a vision of a new temple, the glory of the LORD returning to it (43:4), and a city named The LORD is there (48:35).

themes.title: The glory of God
themes.text: God's glory leaves the sinful temple and later returns, for His presence is the greatest gift to His people.

themes.title: Each person answers to God
themes.text: Every soul belongs to God, and each one is responsible for his own sin; God takes no pleasure in the death of the wicked (18:32).

themes.title: Knowing the LORD
themes.text: Again and again God says that by His judgements and His saving acts people will know that He is the LORD.

themes.title: A new heart and new life
themes.text: God promises to cleanse His people, put His Spirit within them and raise them to new life (37:14).

themes.title: The good Shepherd
themes.text: God will seek His lost sheep and set over them one shepherd, His servant David (34:23).
